name: The St. Regis Lhasa Resort
summary: The St. Regis Lhasa Resort opened in 2010 on Jiangsu Road, about 1.5 km from the Jokhang, as the first international luxury resort in Tibet. It suits travellers who want space, quiet and full-service comfort while adjusting to Lhasa's 3,656 m altitude.
body: The St. Regis sits on Jiangsu Road on the eastern side of central Lhasa, a short drive or a 20–25 minute walk from the Barkhor and Jokhang. Its low-rise buildings in Tibetan style spread around courtyards, with views towards the Potala and the hills from some rooms. Inside, the style mixes Tibetan motifs, dark wood and contemporary design, and rooms are generously sized with heating suited to Lhasa's cold nights.

For our luxury Lhasa and Tibet tours, we choose the St. Regis when clients want the highest level of comfort and service available in the city: restaurants serving Chinese, Tibetan and international food, an indoor pool and spa, and staff used to guests arriving tired from the flight and the altitude. Facilities and dining options can change, so we confirm details at booking. Expect prices well above other Lhasa hotels, especially from May to October.
why: The most complete luxury option in Lhasa, with butler-style service
Quiet setting yet within walking distance of the old town
Spa and indoor pool help with rest days on arrival

faqs.q: How far is the St. Regis Lhasa from the Potala Palace?
faqs.a: The St. Regis is on Jiangsu Road in eastern Lhasa, roughly 1.5 km from the Jokhang and about 3 km from the Potala, around 10 minutes by vehicle. Our guide and driver handle all sightseeing transfers, and the Barkhor is close enough to walk to in the evening if you feel well.

faqs.q: Does the St. Regis Lhasa provide oxygen?
faqs.a: Luxury hotels in Lhasa, including the St. Regis, have generally offered oxygen on request for guests feeling the altitude. Arrangements can change, so we confirm before arrival. Oxygen helps with mild discomfort but is not a substitute for rest, hydration and descending if symptoms are severe.

faqs.q: Can Indian travellers stay at the St. Regis Lhasa on a Kailash yatra?
faqs.a: Yes, on itineraries that pass through Lhasa, such as our Kailash yatra with Lhasa fly-in, the St. Regis can be booked as an upgrade for the Lhasa nights. It does not affect permits. Vegetarian meals are available in the hotel restaurants.

name: Shangri-La Hotel, Lhasa
summary: A large upscale hotel on Norbulingka Road in western Lhasa, within walking distance of the Norbulingka summer palace and a short drive from the Potala. It offers Tibetan-styled rooms, several restaurants and an oxygen lounge, and suits travellers wanting international comfort.
body: The Shangri-La stands at 19 Norbulingka Road, close to the walls of the Norbulingka park and about 1.5 km from the Potala Palace. Its public spaces use Tibetan colours, carved wood and thangka-inspired art, and guest rooms are spacious with heating and large bathrooms. Upper floors on the city side look towards the Potala. The hotel has operated in Lhasa since the mid-2010s and is one of the city's two best-known international luxury hotels.

We use it on premium Lhasa tours and Tibet group tours, often as an alternative to the St. Regis when clients want to be on the Potala and Norbulingka side of town. Guests have praised its breakfast and oxygen lounge, while some recent reviews mention rooms showing their age, so we request renovated rooms where possible. Facilities can change; we confirm what is open at booking.
why: Walk to the Norbulingka and a short drive to the Potala
Oxygen lounge and spa help with altitude on arrival
Wide choice of restaurants including vegetarian options

faqs.q: Where is the Shangri-La Hotel in Lhasa?
faqs.a: At 19 Norbulingka Road in western Lhasa, next to the Norbulingka summer palace and about 1.5 km from the Potala. The Jokhang and Barkhor are about 15 minutes away by car. Lhasa Gonggar airport is about an hour's drive.

faqs.q: Is the Shangri-La or St. Regis better in Lhasa?
faqs.a: Both are luxury hotels. The St. Regis is closer to the old town and Barkhor and has a resort feel; the Shangri-La is beside the Norbulingka and near the Potala, with an oxygen lounge. Choice usually comes down to location and price on your dates. We quote both.

faqs.q: Does the Shangri-La Lhasa serve Indian vegetarian food?
faqs.a: The hotel restaurants offer vegetarian dishes and international buffets, and the kitchen can usually prepare simple Indian-style vegetarian food on request. Choice is narrower than in India. Tell us your dietary needs at booking and we will inform the hotel.

name: Yak Hotel
image_query: Beijing East Road Lhasa old town hotel
summary: A long-running mid-range hotel at 100 Beijing East Road, a few minutes' walk from the Barkhor and Jokhang. Once a backpacker hangout, it now serves tour groups with ensuite rooms and is a practical, central base for value Lhasa tours.
body: The Yak Hotel has been a fixture on Beijing East Road for decades and is mentioned in most guidebooks to Tibet. Its location is the main draw: the Barkhor and Jokhang are about five minutes away on foot, so you can join the evening pilgrim circuit without a vehicle. Rooms range from simple standard twins to larger deluxe rooms, all with private bathrooms and heating. Quality varies between wings, so we request the newer rooms.

We use the Yak on our standard Lhasa tours and Tibet group tours when travellers prefer to stay in the old town at a moderate price. The hotel has a restaurant and Wi-Fi, though many foreign apps are blocked in China. It is a simpler choice than the 5-star hotels, with fewer facilities, but its position in the heart of Lhasa makes up for a lot.
why: Five minutes' walk from the Jokhang and Barkhor
Good value for standard-category Lhasa tours
Familiar to tour groups and Tibetan guides

faqs.q: How far is the Yak Hotel from the Jokhang?
faqs.a: About five minutes on foot. The hotel is on Beijing East Road at the edge of the old town, so the Barkhor circuit and Jokhang square are a short walk away. The Potala is about 2 km west, around 10 minutes by car.

It is a simple 3-star hotel with ensuite rooms, heating and Wi-Fi. Rooms differ in age and quality, so we request renovated rooms. It is clean and practical rather than luxurious; travellers wanting more comfort can upgrade to the St. Regis or Shangri-La.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade from the Yak Hotel on a Lhasa tour?
faqs.a: Yes. Our Lhasa tours price the Yak Hotel or similar as standard, with upgrades to 4-star or 5-star hotels such as the Shangri-La or St. Regis available at extra cost. Upgrades depend on availability, especially from May to October.

name: Gesar Hotel Shigatse
summary: A Tibetan-styled 4-star hotel in Shigatse, also listed as the Xigaze Gesar Hotel, widely used by tour groups on the Lhasa–Gyantse–Shigatse circuit and on the road to Everest and Kailash. Rooms are heated, with Tibetan decor and attached bathrooms.
body: The Gesar Hotel is one of the established upper mid-range hotels in Shigatse, decorated throughout with Tibetan furniture, painted columns and artwork in its lobby and corridors. Rooms are comfortable and heated, with attached bathrooms and hot water, which matters before the colder nights further west at Rongbuk, Saga or Manasarovar. It is a short drive from Tashilhunpo Monastery.

We book the Gesar on our Tibet group tour, Lhasa–Everest tour and Kailash yatra with Lhasa fly-in when available. It has a restaurant serving Chinese and Tibetan dishes and can prepare vegetarian food. Like many hotels in Tibet, its facilities can change between seasons, so we confirm details when we reserve. If the Gesar is full, we use a comparable 4-star hotel in Shigatse.
why: Tibetan-style rooms and public spaces with real character
Heated rooms and hot water before the higher nights west

faqs.q: Is the Gesar Hotel Shigatse a good choice for tours?
faqs.a: Yes. It is one of the hotels most used by tour groups in Shigatse, with Tibetan decor, heated rooms and a restaurant. It is comfortable rather than luxurious. We use it on our Tibet circuits and Lhasa-route Kailash yatras when rooms are available.

faqs.q: How far is the Gesar Hotel from Tashilhunpo?
faqs.a: It is a short drive from Tashilhunpo Monastery, usually 5–10 minutes depending on traffic. Our guide and vehicle handle the transfer, and the monastery visit is scheduled for the morning after arrival or the same afternoon.

faqs.q: Do hotels in Shigatse have oxygen?
faqs.a: Some Shigatse hotels supply oxygen in rooms or at reception, but not all, and arrangements change. Our groups carry their own oxygen in the vehicle. At 3,840 m, most travellers who have already spent nights in Lhasa feel fine.
